off.exclude_keywords_rationale: 'jelly'/'vanilla bean'/'protein powder'/'crisps' come from a real materialized round (LLM_DEVICE=databricks) that independently rediscovered these as needed -- verified against the linking-holdout calibration sample (data/calibration/holdout.parquet, term-matched on 'bean' with no exclusion applied): 'jelly' alone catches 162 jelly-bean-candy rows (branded_food_category='Candy', off tag en:jelly-beans) that 'soybean'/'peanut'/'coffee' don't, since 'jelly bean' doesn't contain any of those substrings. This block previously had no seed entry at all (this one was added retroactively, after the fact -- see README.md's 'Known constraints' TODO about _load_block_holdout falling back to seed_rules.json only, not the block's actual current/best rule), so this list may still be incomplete for records outside what's been checked so far.

beans.notes: this block covers beans in general, not just canned baked beans but also dried beans. It includes black beans, kidney beans, pinto beans, navy beans, etc. It does not include soybeans (which are a separate block), peanuts (which are legumes but not beans), or coffee beans. It also does not include mixed bean salads, dips, or rice and bean dishes, which are separate blocks. Keywords and categories are now AND'd, not OR'd (a record must satisfy both when a rule specifies categories -- see blocking/rules.py's module docstring), so use MORE of the offered category_options on the OFF side than a narrow rule would need under OR semantics -- every specific bean-type category offered (e.g. en:red-beans, en:refried-beans, en:butter-beans, en:canned-black-beans, en:canned-broad-beans, en:beans) should generally be included alongside the ones already picked, not just the highest-count few, since each category you leave out silently drops every OFF record tagged with only that category from the block regardless of how clearly its product name matches. This block does not include FNDDS records which mention fast food, or retaurant.

fndds.exclude_keywords_rationale: Frozen yogurt / yogurt-on-a-cone products are functionally ice cream (a frozen, scooped/soft-serve dessert), not the refrigerated cultured-dairy product this block is about. Verified against the OFF-side yogurt block: 'frozen' excludes 1,271 real frozen-yogurt records; 'cone' excludes only 12 more (mostly already caught by 'frozen' too, e.g. '...frozen yogurt cones'), a couple of which are false positives from an unrelated substring ('Falcone' the surname, 'scones') rather than an actual cone product -- kept anyway per explicit instruction, since the false-positive count is negligible (2 of ~63K OFF block records) next to the real frozen-dessert exclusions.

fndds.keywords_rationale: 'sweet potato'/'pickle' added after verifying against the real FNDDS 'Fried vegetables' category (21 records total): recovers 'Sweet Potato Tots' (3 variants) and 'Pickles, fried'. 'fry'/'fries'/'french fries' were previously excluded (a deliberate scoping choice: battered/breaded PIECES, not potato-fry-style products) but that exclusion was explicitly reversed per instruction -- 'Sweet Potato Fries' (5 variants) and similar are now in scope alongside the tots. 'broccoli'/'okra'/'squash'/'pickle'/'yuca' (bare words, not phrases) added to recover the LAST 5 category records that no phrase-level keyword matched: 'Fried broccoli', 'Fried okra', 'Fried summer squash, yellow or green' (doesn't contain the exact phrase 'fried squash'), 'Pickles, fried' (reversed word order vs. 'fried pickle(s)'), 'Yuca fries'. Safe to add as bare words specifically because they're AND'd with categories=['Fried vegetables'], a curated WWEIA category with only 21 total FNDDS records -- these keywords can only ever narrow *within* that pre-verified set, never pull in an unrelated record from elsewhere in FNDDS. With this addition n_fndds_block reaches the category's full 21/21. (An earlier draft of this file also added several speculative multi-word phrases -- 'fritters', 'fried vegetable(s)', 'fried veggie ...' -- that don't appear verbatim in any of the 21 category records and were dead weight; removed.)

off.exclude_keywords_rationale: 'flavor'/'flavour' added alongside the seafood/cheese excludes once 'onion rings' (bare) replaced the narrower 'onion ring' + category-gate combo below: bare 'onion rings' also catches onion-ring-FLAVORED snack chips ('Sour cream & onion rings flavored corn snack', 'Beer Battered Onion Rings Flavored Potato Chips') which are a different product entirely -- verified this excludes 14 of 679 raw matches, nearly all confirmed flavor-snack products, not real onion rings.
off.keywords_rationale: categories dropped entirely (was: en:breaded-onion-rings/en:pakora/en:frozen-vegetable-tempura/en:battered-onion-rings/en:battered-cauliflower-bites/es:tempuras-de-verduras/en:pakoras) in favor of more precise, longer keyword phrases -- verified real gap: 'Breaded Okra', 'Broccoli fries', 'Yuca Fries', 'Spicy breaded pickle slices' all exist as real, on-topic OFF products but have NO matching category tag at all (mostly just generic 'en:frozen-foods'/'en:frozen-vegetables', shared by countless unrelated products, so can't be added as a category without massive false-positive risk -- and a meaningful share have categories_tags=None entirely, per rules.py's module docstring on OFF's sparse tagging). Since categories AND keywords is deliberately strict (see rules.py), keeping the old category list meant every one of these real products was silently dropped regardless of how clean its keyword match was. Switching to specific multi-word keyword phrases (each checked directly against real product-name samples) keeps precision without needing a category signal that doesn't exist for this block. Verified before/after: 89 -> 665 OFF records, spot-checked a 40-record random sample post-change and found it clean (real breaded/battered/fried vegetable products throughout, plus a couple of borderline-but-genuine items like 'Pakora Dip').
off.categories_rationale: Left empty deliberately -- see keywords_rationale above for why. Do not re-add a category list here without first checking that every keyword phrase it would gate actually has a corresponding OFF category tag covering the on-topic products (most of this block's real long-tail items -- okra, broccoli, yuca, pickle preparations -- don't).

breaded_vegetables.notes: This block covers several distinct vegetables prepared fried/breaded (onion, mushroom, cauliflower, eggplant, squash, green tomato, green bean, broccoli, okra, yuca, pickle, sweet potato, ...), not one single dish -- a record is in-block if it's ANY of these, so don't narrow the keyword/category lists down to only the vegetable(s) that happen to dominate the samples you're shown. Consider exploring variables detecting tempura or pakora-style products, which are a distinct preparation style from the more generic battered/breaded-fried vegetables. The OFF side is deliberately broad (no category gate -- see off.categories_rationale for why), to catch all the many ways breaded/fried vegetables can be described in product names, but it excludes breaded seafood/cheese products (shrimp, tilapia, haddock, flounder, mozzarella sticks, fish sticks) and onion-ring-FLAVORED snack chips/crisps, neither of which are in scope.
